sub_indicators.label: International standards for information technology and data
sub_indicators.subject: gov.standards
sub_indicators.text: Adoption of international standards: international standards for information technology and data
sub_indicators.norm_short: The AfCFTA annex on technical barriers to trade, Article 6(2), commits its parties to adopt or adapt international standards, and the African Union's Digital Transformation Strategy asks for rules in line with international norms. Neither names the standards.
criteria: A source from the past three years says the country belongs to no international standards organisation.

The country's standards body is a member of ISO, the International Organization for Standardization, or of IEC, its counterpart for electrical technology. Full, correspondent and subscriber members all count. Membership of the African or a regional standards organisation does not.

The country has adopted an international standard on information technology or data as a national standard: a named ISO, IEC or ITU standard on information technology, information security, software or data. A count of adopted standards that names none, a draft, and a standard in another field do not count.

Public bodies must meet a named international standard: a law, decree, regulation, directive or circular names an international standard on information technology or data and requires ministries, agencies or government systems to meet it. A rule for one sector, a text modelled on a standard, and a system built to one do not count.

The country has taken part in writing international standards on information technology in the past three years: a dated source names the standards body or a public body as a participating member, chair or secretariat of an ISO or IEC committee on information technology or data. An observer seat does not count.
